methods.label: Recognize the vector approach
methods.explanation: The investigation itself is not described here. Among the displayed choices, A states the relevant mathematical idea: triangle sides can be represented by vectors, whose magnitudes give their lengths. For two side vectors \(\mathbf{u}\) and \(\mathbf{v}\) with included angle \(\theta\), the relation \(\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|\cos\theta\) connects lengths and angles. Magnitudes and dot products can be computed from coordinates, turning these geometric relationships into coordinate calculations. Thus the supported choice is A.
